title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier‑Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether deterministic verification plus a bounded LLM‑guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier‑detected semantic invariant violations in intent→device‑configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks; 12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks), a single generator/prompt pairing (gpt‑5‑mini), and a pybatfish‑style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared‑initial‑candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired‑bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed archived). Two preregistration/analysis issues bounded inference: (1) executed shared‑generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per‑condition generation, and (2) a prespecified comparison versus a schema‑constrained baseline was not executed in the archived run. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no additional verifier‑detectable benefit when the generator+prompting pairing already yielded verifier‑acceptable candidates on this synthetic workload. We release and analyze the archived artifacts and recommend reproducible follow‑ups (independent per‑condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi‑model runs, and expanded verifier coverage).

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) promise to reduce NetOps workload by translating high‑level intent into device configurations, but stochastic generation can produce syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect artifacts that violate operational invariants (reachability, required workflow order, security predicates). Prior work therefore recommends architectures that interpose deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects prior to execution. Unresolved empirical questions include whether bounded GVR reduces verifier‑detected semantic violations in paired, controlled evaluations and how evaluation semantics (shared vs independent generation) affect measurable benefit. We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment addressing: Does deterministic verification plus a bounded LLM‑guided repair loop (GVR) reduce verifier‑detected semantic invariant violations relative to (A) unconstrained generation and (B) schema‑constrained decoding on a public synthetic NetOps task bank, under the frozen data, model, and validator? Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired evaluation (N = 240 paired tasks) using gpt‑5‑mini and a deterministic pybatfish‑style validator; (2) transparent execution accounting showing shared‑initial‑candidate semantics produced one generation per task reused across arms (model_calls_used = 240) and that every generation satisfied the verifier (n11 = 240); (3) confirmatory statistics reporting a degenerate null (paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired‑bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples) and reconciliation of preregistered power assumptions with executed semantics; and (4) operational recommendations (independent per‑condition generation, adversarial injections, multi‑model evaluations, and expanded verifier coverage) grounded in the archived artifacts.
sections.related_work: Three bodies of verified literature ground our study. First, cross‑domain surveys and empirical studies document LLM hallucinations and fabricated outputs for code and structured artifacts, motivating deterministic validators and verification gates in downstream pipelines. These works show that unconstrained generative outputs can be syntactically plausible while violating deeper, domain‑specific invariants. Second, generate–verify–repair and constrained decoding techniques improve mechanically checkable properties (compilation, grammar validity) in code and DSL generation tasks; case studies report reduced surface‑level failures but do not uniformly quantify semantic correctness for domain‑specific invariants. Third, NetOps research emphasizes verifier‑driven evaluation (reachability and policy invariants), intent‑based translation systems, and human‑in‑the‑loop governance for high‑stakes changes. Our run differs from prior work in three ways: it is preregistered and archived before execution; it uses a paired confirmatory design with a frozen analysis executor; and it evaluates verifier‑detectable semantic violations (not only syntactic/executable correctness) on a structured synthetic task bank with deterministic validator predicates.
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration: The study was preregistered with a frozen analysis plan and explicit estimands. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired difference in verifier‑detected semantic‑violation rates). Two prespecified primary comparisons were listed: GVR vs unconstrained (C vs A) and GVR vs schema‑constrained decoding (C vs B) with Bonferroni correction across these two comparisons. The analysis executor was frozen prior to execution.

Task bank and oracle: The public synthetic NetOps task bank (archived task manifest) encodes initial device states, intents, workflow constraints, and expected final states; tasks are stratified into 12 topology/policy clusters with 20 tasks each (N = 240). The deterministic verifier implements pybatfish‑style checks and returns structured diagnostics (violation_count, violation list, parsed_command_count, required_command_count). Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation as implemented by deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Intervention and frozen execution semantics: The archival execution used an adapter orchestration family that implemented shared_initial_candidate generation semantics: one generated candidate per task was produced and reused across arms (model_calls_used = 240). The guarded arm (C) interposes the deterministic verifier and, when the verifier indicates a violation, allows a single bounded LLM‑guided repair attempt (maximum one repair call per task). The baseline arm (A) presented generated output without repair. The preregistration had planned an analogous paired experiment comparing GVR to a schema‑constrained baseline (B), but that comparison was not executed in the archived run (see Results and Disclosure). All seeds, task manifests, model configuration, and execution manifests are archived.

Statistical plan and power: The preregistered power plan targeted an absolute paired reduction of 10 percentage points with N = 240 under the assumption of independent per‑condition generation; the registered paired analysis executor performs an exact McNemar‑style test and computes absolute risk reduction with bootstrap confidence intervals. The executed shared‑generation semantics remove independent per‑condition stochasticity and therefore invalidate the preregistered power calculation for the observed run; this mismatch is recorded in the archived execution manifest and is central to interpretation.
sections.results:
Execution accounting: The run completed all planned episodes (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; failed_episode_count = 0). Provider audit recorded model_calls_used = 240 under shared generation semantics. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm consistent episode accounting and that a single shared initial candidate was used for each pair (see archived execution and response artifacts).

Primary confirmatory outcome: Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic validator in both arms. Contingency counts were: n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired‑bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_resamples = 10,000; seed archived). Analysis artifacts (paired contingency table, condition summary, bootstrap log) are archived and authoritative for these numbers.

Repair usage and diagnostics: The guarded arm never invoked the repair loop because validation_after indicated violation_count = 0 for every task; repair_applied = false for all episodes. Representative per‑task scoring JSON and validator_trace blocks show identical shared_initial_candidate and final_configuration for baseline and guarded conditions, and validator_id deterministic_netops_validator_v5 returned valid = true in every case.

Degenerate inference: The absence of within‑pair discordant outcomes makes the paired test degenerate: no within‑pair disagreements exist to estimate a differential effect. The exact‑test p = 1.00 and the collapsed bootstrap CI are deterministic consequences of observed contingency under the preregistered analysis methods. Importantly, this degeneracy stems from two artifact‑supported mechanisms: (1) distributional alignment where the generator+prompt pairing satisfied the validator across the synthetic task bank, and (2) shared_initial_candidate semantics that removed independent per‑condition stochastic variation and therefore removed discordance potential the GVR intervention could exploit.

Unexecuted prespecified comparison: The preregistration specified two primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B). The archived execution artifacts document only the adapter‑configured paired experiment comparing unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared_initial_candidate semantics; the prespecified schema‑constrained baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. We disclose this as a prespecified but unexecuted comparison and an unresolved procedural limitation.
sections.discussion:
Conservative interpretation and operational meaning: Artifact‑grounded results show bounded GVR added no verifier‑detectable benefit in this specific configuration because no verifier‑detected errors were present to correct. This outcome does not imply GVR is ineffective in general; rather, it illustrates two points critical for operational evaluation: (1) verification sensitivity depends on the verifier's coverage and the task distribution, and (2) evaluation semantics (shared vs independent generation) determine whether an experiment has power to detect generation‑dependent interventions. For practitioners, these findings imply that measuring the marginal value of GVR requires evaluation designs that (a) allow independent per‑condition generation to preserve stochastic discordance, (b) include adversarial or golden tasks that reliably elicit verifier failures, or (c) expand verifier predicates to reduce oracle incompleteness.

Threats to validity: Internal validity: the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per‑condition generation; the executed shared‑generation semantics violated that assumption and therefore invalidate that power argument for the observed run. Construct validity: passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 confirms only the encoded invariants; unencoded operational risks may remain. External validity: results derive from one synthetic task bank, one generator (gpt‑5‑mini), a single bounded repair budget (one attempt), and one verifier implementation; generalization to vendor syntax, production topologies, or other LLM families is not supported. Conclusion validity: zero discordant outcomes preclude evidence for GVR efficacy under the executed semantics.

Recommendations for reproducible follow‑ups (artifact‑grounded): (1) Re‑execute the preregistered paired design with independent per‑condition generation (set independent_condition_generation = true) using the archived task manifest and RNG seeds to restore discordance potential. (2) Inject adversarial/golden tasks (the preregistration planned a 10% golden subset) whose expected verifier outcome is known to validate verifier sensitivity. (3) Expand model scope beyond gpt‑5‑mini to measure cross‑model generality. (4) Allow larger or iterative repair budgets to measure repair iteration distributions. (5) Broaden verifier coverage (additional semantic invariants or symbolic/SMT hybrids) to address oracle incompleteness. The archived artifacts include the task manifest, model configuration, and adapter configuration required to deterministically reproduce and extend the run.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired experiment evaluating bounded GVR on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared‑initial‑candidate semantics and for the supplied task bank and verifier, every generated candidate passed the deterministic validator in both arms (n11 = 240), yielding a null paired estimate and degenerate statistics (exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired‑bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no verifier‑detectable benefit in this specific, artifact‑grounded setting because there were no verifier‑detectable errors to correct. Two preregistration/execution deviations limit inference: the executed shared‑generation semantics invalidated the independent‑generation power assumption, and a prespecified schema‑constrained comparison was not executed. We publish the authoritative archived artifacts and recommend deterministic reruns that restore independent per‑condition generation, inject adversarial tasks, expand generator coverage, and broaden verifier predicates to more robustly assess GVR’s operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish‑style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor‑specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared‑generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model‑call cost but also removed per‑arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per‑condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per‑condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single‑model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt‑5‑mini); cross‑model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema‑constrained baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
